description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the redevelopment of Luciline, a 9-hectare former industrial area along the Seine in Rouen, France, into an eco-district combining climate adaptation and mitigation. The plan provides about 1,000 homes, 30,000 square metres of offices and almost 20,000 square metres of commercial space. Rainwater runs through small canals into wide vegetated ditches, a larger canal and the Seine; buried water courses were reopened; 3 hectares, about 30% of the site, are green public space; many buildings have green roofs; and total building footprint is capped at 135,000 square metres to limit the urban heat island. A heat network uses water drawn from 4 to 5 metres deep in the Seine for heating and cooling, backed by gas boilers, and the first passive building opened in 2014. Coverage: one district of Rouen, with milestones from the 2006 concession to expected completion in 2030. Access: the case study page, first published in 2016 and last modified 2026-08-25, plus city and developer sites. Licence: Climate-ADAPT content under the EEA reuse policy; free. Caveats: this is a descriptive account from the developer and an EEA study, with costs and benefits reported but no measured flood or heat performance. Simulation uses are a documented design reference for modelling blue-green drainage and heat island measures in dense brownfield districts. Related records: the cross-cutting piece's Climate-ADAPT case study records.

outcomes: A 9-hectare former industrial site on the Seine is being rebuilt as an eco-district with open canals and vegetated ditches draining rainfall to the Seine, 3 hectares of green public space, green roofs, a building footprint capped at 135,000 square metres and a river-water heating and cooling network; half the buildings were complete in 2020 and completion is expected in 2030. Total cost is about EUR 50 million, of which the city invested 28 million.
